newsitem.title: USA: Array of foreign crudes beckoning U.S. refiners.
newsitem.headline: Array of foreign crudes beckoning U.S. refiners.

text.p: An array of foreign crudes continued to beckon U.S. Gulf Coast refiners Wednesday, although few deals were heard transacted amid slack demand, traders said.
The spread between February West Texas Intermediate and North Sea Brent stood around $1.70-80 a barrel, fueling a wave of transatlantic offers.
A Brent cargo for arrival February 1-5 was heard offered at February WTI minus 40 cents on a delivered basis, traders said.
"The spread's blowing out. There's more barrels out there than people originally thought," one Texas trader said.
West African barrels were also looking for a home, with Cabinda for January 25-27 on offer at February WTI minus 85 cents on a delivered basis, traders said.
Even Russian Urals is available. Glencore is asking February WTI minus $1.65 on a delivered basis, although the timing was unclear. Taurus was also heard to have two Urals cargoes on offer.
The flurry of foreign offers has depressed domestic sweet crude prices, traders said.
Meanwhile, the first Iraqi oil to hit the U.S. spot crude market since sanctions were imposed over six years ago was recently sold by trading firm Bayoil, traders confirmed.
Bayoil has sold two Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs) totalling four million barrels of Basrah Light on a delivered basis to Gulf Coast refiners, including Clark and Mobil, traders said.
Houston-based Bayoil has a six-month contract with Iraq for 30,000 barrels per day (bpd) under the U.N. oil-for-food program that started December 10.
Under Iraqi crude contract terms, Bayoil buys at a $3.75 per barrel discount to WTI, with the actual price set against WTI prices for five business days starting 15 days after the ship sails.

After shipping, insurance, offloading and related costs, traders estimate that Bayoil made a margin of about 70 cents a barrel, assuming the delivered price was similar to the $1.65 discount to WTI which Russian Urals crude is selling for in the U.S., traders said.
Latin American activity was subdued. Conoco was heard to have some surplus Oriente that could possibly be resold at WTI minus $2.40 a barrel cif.
Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol is testing the waters for a possible offer of Vasconia crude for late January, traders said.
In the U.S. aftermarket, a series of partial paper February Brents changed hands at $24.74-80, six cents off the IPE settlement on the low side.
Brent Feb/March traded at 55 cents, down five cents from the London close.
